San Francisco author and atheist activist David Fitzgerald argues that Jesus may have been a literary figure combining stories of several people and religious traditions in first-century Judea.
Fitzgerald says the Gospels were written decades after Jesus’s supposed life and that contemporary historical accounts do not mention him.

Researchers at Johns Hopkins Medical School in Baltimore found that damage to the right sagittal stratum can impair the ability to recognise sarcasm.
In a study published in *Neurocase*, 24 stroke patients listened to sincere and sarcastic sentences while undergoing brain scans.
Five patients with significant damage to the area identified only 22 per cent of sarcastic comments, compared with 50 per cent among those without damage.
The researchers said the findings could help guide rehabilitation and help families avoid misunderstandings when communicating with stroke survivors.

A CDC study released Thursday found that about 30 percent of U.S. women had another pregnancy within 18 months of giving birth, though experts recommend waiting at least that long.
Based on 2011 birth certificates from 36 states and Washington, D.C., the report covered about 83 percent of U.S. births.

The CDC said this was its first report on pregnancy spacing, so researchers do not know whether spacing has changed over time.

Indonesia has the most threatened mammals, with 184, followed by Madagascar with 114 and Mexico with 101, according to maps created by London-based The Eco Experts using World Bank data.
Deforestation puts Indonesian species, including orangutans, Sumatran tigers and rhinos, at risk; the country’s rainforests occupy 1 per cent of Earth’s land but host 12 per cent of its mammal species.
Madagascar’s threatened mammals include lemurs, while habitat loss in Mexico threatens species such as the vaquita, with fewer than 100 reportedly remaining in the wild.
A Lancaster University survey in Borba and Novo Aripuanã found that many households eat rainforest wildlife, including some species classified as threatened.

The study, published in *Conservation Letters*, says expanding plantations threaten endangered gibbons, leopards and elephants in Southeast Asia.

Campaigners are urging the UK government to implement the Easter Act 1928, fixing Easter Sunday between April 9 and 15 to help businesses and families plan.

North Pacific gray whale Varvara swam nearly 14,000 miles, setting a record for the longest mammal migration ever recorded, according to an Oregon State University study.
She traveled from feeding grounds off Russia’s Sakhalin Island across the Pacific and down the US West Coast to Baja, Mexico.
Researchers say her visit to three eastern gray whale breeding areas suggests she may be an eastern gray, rather than an endangered western gray.
The findings could mean fewer than the estimated 150 western gray whales remain and warrant closer study of the whales’ genetics.

Chernomorets could face relegation and disqualification from UEFA competitions if it fails to settle its debts.
The club, 11th in the 14-team league, was due to travel to Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk on Wednesday.

Police in Tulsa County, Oklahoma, intercepted a package containing about $30,000 worth of meth hidden inside an Easter bunny.
A police dog helped detect the drugs, which were packed in two condoms inside the toy.
The package was headed to Carolyn Ross’s home in Tahlequah, where police arrested her.
Ross reportedly admitted knowing about the drugs and said she was to redistribute them; she is held on $75,000 bond.

Researchers in Tokyo found that Long-Evans rats can recognise pain in other rats’ facial expressions and use that information to make decisions.
In a study published in *Royal Society Open Science*, rats spent about a minute less in a room displaying images of pained rats than in one showing neutral expressions.
The researchers said the findings suggest rats’ pain expressions may communicate distress, warn others of danger or prompt them to help.

Jack Grealish hopes to turn past Wembley defeats into victory when Aston Villa face Liverpool in the FA Cup semi-final on April 19.
The 19-year-old made his first Premier League start against Queens Park Rangers on Tuesday and hopes to keep his place.

Grealish says Christian Benteke’s return to form gives Villa hope of avoiding relegation.

A fire destroyed Baltimore’s $16 million Mary Harvin Transformation Center after riots following Freddie Gray’s funeral on Monday; its cause remains under investigation.
The East Baltimore project was planned to include about 60 senior apartments and services such as job training, counseling and support for people with HIV and AIDS.
Church leaders said poverty, unemployment and long-standing neglect fueled community anger, and vowed to rebuild the center, which was expected to open in November or December.
The Woda Group reaffirmed its commitment to rebuilding, while a church architecture firm offered free design help.

Ciudad Real airport in Spain, built for €1.1 billion and opened in 2009, closed in April 2012 after its operators fell into financial difficulties.
After failing to attract buyers at an asking price of €100 million, the airport is now offered for one pound, though buyers would inherit hundreds of millions of pounds in debt.
Designed to serve Madrid and the Andalusian coast and handle five million passengers a year, the airport now stands empty.
Its final commercial flight was operated by Vueling in October 2011, and the 4,000-metre runway still requires maintenance.

An Arctic airmass from Iceland is expected to bring colder, unsettled weather to Britain from Saturday, after an unusually warm April.
Temperatures are forecast to fall by around 10C next week, reaching 8C in the north and 12–14C in the south, with overnight lows possibly below freezing.
The Met Office predicts rain and possible thunderstorms in London during Sunday’s marathon, with heavy downpours also possible.
Forecasters say the cold spell could make the end of April feel like a return to winter.

Steve Tempest-Mitchell, 56, from Bradford, lost 16 stone after gastric bypass surgery 14 months ago, dropping from 32 stone to 16.
He chose surgery after struggling to control his Type 2 diabetes and becoming almost housebound.
His weight had risen during years of demanding work, including bomb-disposal contracting in Iraq and Afghanistan from 1996 to 2005.
Now a grandfather, he says he has more energy to play with his grandchildren.
